claim: Bank of Russia reported on 25 October 2021 that the current-account surplus reached an all-time high in 2021 Q3, driven by faster export growth and high global commodity prices, with some support from eased OPEC+ oil-production restrictions.
limitations: Shows strong external-resource generation before invasion; does not establish how export earnings were allocated or converted into military capability.

claim: Bank of Russia historical reserve data show international reserves above USD 600 billion through much of late 2021, including USD 622.8 billion on 3 December and USD 630.6 billion on 31 December 2021.
limitations: The current webpage is maintained retrospectively; original week-by-week public release timing must be verified before using any value at an earlier cutoff. Reserves are not equivalent to spendable war finance.

claim: On 27 January 2022 the Bank of Russia stated that the 2021 current-account surplus had reached an all-time high, primarily because export values surged with global commodity prices.
limitations: Admissible only for late-January/February 2022 snapshots; not for December 2021 cutoffs. Does not identify military allocation.

claim: EEAS later reported that in the final three months before 24 February 2022 its East Stratcom Task Force observed a distinctive spike in pro-Kremlin disinformation narratives about Ukraine, including sharp increases in 'Nazi' and 'genocide' framing.
limitations: Strong retrospective evidence that the information layer changed, but publication is post-invasion. It must not be injected into earlier snapshots unless contemporaneous source records are reconstructed from the underlying repository.

claim: EEAS states that EU institutional capabilities to identify and respond to Russian disinformation had been built since 2015 in the context of aggression against Ukraine, establishing that a dedicated observation mechanism existed before the 2021-2022 crisis.
limitations: This establishes sensor/institution existence, not the content, scale or causal effect of any specific 2021 campaign.
